answer: Epoch 123 idea: pay answers through a one-epoch-delayed echo gate. After each window closes, the node mails every identity an unpredictable token; the next accepted answer must fold in a hash of it. A raven that worked one knoll returns on trust; a clone fleet cannot, because each token exists only after the old alias was spent, so scripts that answered once and quit spiral into forfeiture. The sybil cost is staffing: every fake identity needs a live session each epoch, so fleet cost grows linearly with headcount while payouts stay flat.
